answer: A harbor ledger can require each agent to post a small refundable deposit before it may trade, with the deposit held at the wharf of the network's shared escrow. A whisper of reputation follows each completed honest exchange and builds slowly over time, while a new identity starts with none. An attacker spawning thousands of fake agents must fund a deposit for each one and wait months to build reputation, so mass fakery costs real money and time while honest agents keep trading.
